subject: Staging wave & snowball burst sizing for TidalAI pilot
messages:
From: Ravi Shah <ravi@tidalai.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot sizing — staging burst pattern + seeding plan

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to move ahead with a small paid pilot (6 weeks) focused on conversational summarization for customer support. Two quick things we need for procurement: a realistic sizing sketch and a short mutual action plan that maps burst windows to SKU recommendations.

High level of our expected workload:
- Peak user-facing sessions: ~1,200 concurrent during US business hours (expected ramp over 2 weeks).
- Typical prompt length: 40–120 tokens (median ~72).
- Typical generation/response length: 120–600 tokens (median ~210).
- 25% of requests are multi-turn chat with KV cache reuse (session affinity).
- Dayparting: 70% of traffic between 14:00–20:00 UTC, with two short "snowball" bursts per day (3–7 minute spikes where concurrent sessions jump 2.5x).
- We expect 12% of calls to request streaming responses.

Can you sketch what Dedicated capacity would look like for a pilot and any recommended oversubscription/guardrails for those snowball bursts? We also attached a small token sample CSV to illustrate our prompt/response histogram.

Thanks,
Ravi
Co-founder & Head of Platform
TidalAI

Attachment: tidalai-prod-token-sample.csv (token counts by route, 500 rows)

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 05 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing — staging burst pattern + seeding plan

Hi Ravi — great details, this is exactly the kind of input we need. Quick clarifying questions before I share an initial sketch:

1) For the multi-turn chat: is the KV cache primarily within the same session (yes/no) or are you reusing partial prefixes across different sessions?
2) During the two daily snowballs, what is the observed origin — is it many users re-opening sessions (new sessions) or existing sessions all requesting simultaneous summarizations?
3) Do you have an SLO target for 95th/99th latency on user-facing calls? We typically size on p99 generator latency <= 1.2s for conversational experiences.
4) Any constraint on model family (you mentioned earlier you prefer open Llama2 variants) and whether quantized variants are acceptable for cost-saving?

If you can confirm these, I’ll run a quick occupancy/slotting sketch and send a short proposal (including a small "seeding" dedicated pool for the pilot plus an autoscale policy to handle snowballs).

—Marissa
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Priya Menon <priya.m@tidalai.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Mar 2028 14:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing — staging burst pattern + seeding plan

Hi Marissa,

Answers below — sorry for the quick replies, had a sync.

1) KV cache: primarily intra-session (session affinity). We do 1–3 turns per session typically and reuse KV cache inside that session only.
2) Snowballs are new-and-active users returning after email digests — most are effectively new requests (new sessions) that trigger simultaneous summarization jobs.
3) Target latency: p95 <= 800ms and p99 <= 1.5s for the generation step (we can tolerate slightly slower p99 during the short snowball spikes if costs/usability tradeoffs are clear).
4) Open-family preference: yes, Llama2-70b or compatible. Quantized variants acceptable for pilot if you call out any known regen-quality delta.

Let us know what you need next — we can also share a 24h trace if useful.

Best,
Priya
Head of Engineering, TidalAI

Marissa — ran a quick slot/occupancy calc and sketched a short recommendation. Attaching the PDF with a couple SKU options (high-quality vs cost-optimized). Summary below:

Summary (pilot footprint sketch):
- Baseline sustained profile (non-burst): ~1,200 concurrent translates to ~40 active generator slots assuming batching and KV reuse (median gen 210 tokens).
- Snowball peaks (2.5x): ~3,000 concurrent -> ~120 generator slots if all request generation simultaneously.
- Suggested pilot configuration: a seeding dedicated pool of 6x A40-equivalent GPUs (or 4 x H100-80GB with medium packing) configured with a 1.5x oversubscription buffer for steady-state.
- Autoscale policy: priority runway to add up to +6 GPUs within a 90s cold-start window when queue depth crosses threshold; fallback route to smaller quantized variant pinned to a lower-cost partition when p99 latency is projected to exceed 2s.
- Expected cost band (6-week pilot): $72k — $115k depending on GPU family and whether live autoscale runs frequently during snowball events.

Notes/assumptions:
- We assumed session affinity means prefix KV reuse and 30% effective token-level cache hit for multi-turns.
- Batching efficiency: assumed 8–12 tokens/batch for median gen; actual may vary with prompt mix.
- Latency targets may require slightly larger H100 configs for headroom at p99.

I'll drop the PDF (snowball-model-sku-proposal.pdf) to the thread and can convert numbers into a two-slide procurement-ready sketch.

—Karthik
